## Overview

Environmental suitability testing (Test for environmental suitability) is a key verification process in the system integration and verification testing phase (P15), corresponding to node P15.2.3 in the WBS. Through systematic tests of environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, dust, electromagnetic interference, lighting, and floor material, it verifies the robustness of humanoid robots in target operating environments and exposes environment-sensitive defects. What it truly changes is not the functional verification of "whether it can run," but the qualification determination of "whether it can still work reliably when the environment changes."

## Overview

Software stability and regression testing is a critical verification process in the humanoid robot full-system integration and validation testing phase (P15). Its core task is to ensure that the robot does not crash or experience functional degradation under long-duration operation, anomaly injection, and version iteration. This method employs long-duration operation, stress testing, fault injection, and version regression as its primary tools, with "no crashes during long-duration operation and successful recovery from critical fault injections" as the completion criteria. It serves as the quality gate connecting durability testing and certification preparation.

ent_method_hardware_in_the_loop.summary: A validation method where real hardware controllers interact with a real-time simulation of the plant, enabling safe and repeatable testing of control software.
ent_method_hardware_in_the_loop.body:
## Overview

Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing is a method that connects a real hardware controller to a real-time simulation model of the plant, verifying the correctness and performance of control software in a closed loop. What it truly changes is not the "test location," but the "timing and risk structure of testing"—it allows control software to run on real processors with real timing before a physical prototype exists, thereby shifting catastrophic failures from the field to the laboratory. HIL sits in the middle of the assembly integration testing domain (domain 04), serving as a critical verification layer connecting pure simulation (SIL/MIL) with full-machine physical testing.

## Overview

Performance benchmarking is a systematic testing method used in the Integration & V&V phase to verify whether a product's key performance indicators (KPIs) meet design specifications. What it truly changes is not the simple verification of "whether it can run," but rather the qualification process of "transforming subjective descriptions in the PRD into traceable engineering evidence using quantifiable acceptance criteria." This method targets dimensions such as walking speed, battery life, payload, operational precision, and noise, verifying KPIs item by item against the PRD, and ultimately outputs the "Performance Test Report" and KPI compliance rate.

ent_method_calibration_joint_camera_imu.body:
## Overview

Joint-Camera-IMU Calibration is a key preliminary method in multi-sensor fusion for humanoid robots, used to precisely estimate the spatial transformation relationships (extrinsic parameters) between cameras, LiDAR, and IMUs. In humanoid robots, cameras provide dense texture and semantic information, LiDAR provides precise 3D geometry, and IMUs provide high-frequency motion states. Only when the three work together can functions such as RGB point cloud coloring, deep fusion, and 3D target localization be achieved. What it truly changes is not the calibration accuracy of a single sensor, but rather the fusion paradigm that moves heterogeneous sensors from "working independently" to a "unified spatiotemporal reference frame."

## Overview
Safety function testing is a critical process node in the whole-machine integration and verification testing phase (P15) that verifies the robot's safety mechanisms operate as designed, corresponding to WBS number P15.2.1. It validates that the robot can safely shut down or enter a protective posture under any abnormal condition through means such as emergency stop, fall protection, collision detection, limit switches, and safety zones. Its completion criterion is the issuance of a safety test report and confirmation that all safety functions pass. What it truly changes is not the troubleshooting action of "detecting faults," but the qualification process of "proving that the safety design holds through quantifiable acceptance criteria."

The Joint Calibration Procedure is a systematic method for determining the absolute zero position, encoder offset, and direction flag of each actuator after assembly. What it truly changes is not the operational methods on the assembly floor, but the credibility of the kinematic model as it moves from paper to physical reality.

ent_paper_neves_a_collaborative_robot_as.body:
## Overview
This study evaluates the effectiveness of collaborative robots in coexistence, collaboration, and synergy modes by comparing manual and robot-assisted assembly of roller conveyor sections. The experiment utilized a KUKA LBR iiwa 7 R800 robotic arm and a SCHUNK Co-act EGP-C 64 gripper, and the results showed that collaborative operations significantly improved ergonomic conditions and reduced operators' mental workload, although assembly time increased by approximately 15%. The robot operation was intuitive and easy to use, guiding users to follow the correct sequence of procedures.

ent_paper_team_reconfiguration_algorithm.summary: Introduces a realistic "loose sliding-cubes" model for unit-cube modular robots that captures mechanical alignment features and passive modules handled by external robots, and proves two constructive universality results: a plane-sweep algorithm using Θ(n) auxiliary modules and a monotone construction for polycubes with external feature size at least 2.
ent_paper_team_reconfiguration_algorithm.body:
## Overview
We introduce and analyze a model for self-reconfigurable robots made up of unit-cube modules. Compared to past models, our model aims to newly capture two important practical aspects of real-world robots. First, modules often do not occupy an exact unit cube, but rather have features like bumps extending outside the allotted space so that modules can interlock. Thus, for example, our model forbids modules from squeezing in between two other modules that are one unit distance apart. Second, our model captures the practical scenario of many passive modules assembled by a single robot, instead of requiring all modules to be able to move on their own. ent_paper_gheorghe_integration_testing_o.name: Integration Testing of Heterotic Systems
ent_paper_gheorghe_integration_testing_o.summary: This paper proposes a formal framework based on communicating stream X-machine systems (CSXMS) for modelling heterogeneous systems composed of radically different technologies, and derives an automatic test-set generation strategy for integration testing.
ent_paper_gheorghe_integration_testing_o.body:
## 概述

本文提出一种针对异质系统（如硅基计算与湿件生物组件组合）的集成测试策略，通过将系统建模为通信流 X 机系统（CSXMS）并转换为单一 SXM 以复用标准测试方法。核心贡献在于给出形式化转换框架与可测试性条件，并以 P 系统与 SXM 组合为例演示，但未提供实验验证。

## 它改变了什么

异质系统测试的真正难点不在单一组件，而在组件间交互可能产生超出各部分能力之和的行为——如量子簇态计算机中两层交互对整体能力有根本贡献。既有 SXM 测试理论假设“下一步”概念清晰，但连续实时交互系统（如纳米机器人群体）中该假设失效。本文试图将异质系统纳入 SXM 框架，使测试集生成策略可推广至更一般场景，而非仅为特定实例设计测试。

作者改变的关键认知是：集成测试不必模拟组件全部内部行为，可将组件视为黑盒，仅关注交互接口。这大幅简化了 DFT 条件的满足难度，因为无需验证组件内部正确性（已在单元测试阶段处理），只需保证交互行为可观测、可区分。

## 方法拆解

### 建模框架
- 将异质系统表示为 CSXMS，每个组件是带输入端口（IN）与输出端口（OUT）的通信 SXM（CSXM）。
- 配置变化分两类：普通变化（无通信，机器消费输入符号或保持 λ）与通信变化（符号从一台机器输出端口移至另一台输入端口，目标端口须为空）。

### 转换为单一 SXM（P^T）
- 为每个通信函数引入额外输入符号 a（通信事件）与输出符号 [i,j]（表示应用了 Π_i 的通信函数 φ_j''）。
- 输入字母表：In = ((In_1 ∪ {a, null}) × ... × (In_n ∪ {a, null})) \ {(null, ..., null)}
- 输出字母表：Out = ((Out_1 ∪ {[1,j] | j≠1} ∪ {null}) × ... × (Out_n …

ent_paper_brown_optimal_sequential_task_.body:
## Overview
We study the problem of sequential task assignment and collision-free routing for large teams of robots in applications with inter-task precedence constraints (e.g., task $A$ and task $B$ must both be completed before task $C$ may begin). Such problems commonly occur in assembly planning for robotic manufacturing applications, in which sub-assemblies must be completed before they can be combined to form the final product. We propose a hierarchical algorithm for computing makespan-optimal solutions to the problem. The algorithm is evaluated on a set of randomly generated problem instances where robots must transport objects between stations in a "factory "grid world environment. ent_paper_rojas_robot_contact_task_state.summary: This paper converts 3D Cartesian end-effector trajectories into high-level action grammars through Frenet-frame segmentation and Direct Curve Coding, then uses linear SVMs to classify robot behaviors and verify task output, achieving 86% task-output verification and 72% behavior-monitoring accuracy on snap-assembly tasks in simulation and on a real HIRO-NX dual-arm humanoid robot.
ent_paper_rojas_robot_contact_task_state.body:
## Overview
Uncertainty is a major difficulty in endowing robots with autonomy. Robots often fail due to unexpected events. In robot contact tasks are often design to empirically look for force thresholds to define state transitions in a Markov chain or finite state machines. Such design is prone to failure in unstructured environments, when due to external disturbances or erroneous models, such thresholds are met, and lead to state transitions that are false-positives. The focus of this paper is to perform high-level state estimation of robot behaviors and task output for robot contact tasks. Our approach encodes raw low-level 3D cartesian trajectories and converts them into a high level (HL) action grammars. ent_equipment_system_integration_test_be.body:
## Overview

The System Integration Test Bench is a physical testing platform used before final assembly to verify joint performance, communication buses, control loops, and safety systems. What it truly changes is not "whether testing exists," but rather shifts fault detection in humanoid robots from the "full-system integration phase" to the "component integration phase," enabling single-joint performance verification, bus timing verification, and safety logic verification to proceed in parallel without full-system risk.
